name: SnapTrade
summary: Read-only brokerage accounts (Wealthsimple, Questrade, and others) through a SnapTrade Personal API key the user creates. The user links brokerages in SnapTrade's own portal, so Heiwa never sees a brokerage password. Heiwa's client is GET-only and has no trading or money-movement path.
revocation_path: Delete the Personal API key and unlink brokerages at https://dashboard.snaptrade.com; `heiwa connect snaptrade --disconnect` removes the local copy of the key.

source_notes.title: SnapTrade Personal vs Commercial API keys

capabilities.description: List brokerage accounts with the brokerage-reported total and per-currency cash. Only the last four characters of an account number are stored.
capabilities.rate_hint: 250 requests/minute per client; 10 requests/minute per account for Personal keys where enforced.

capabilities.description: Read positions per account: symbol, units, last price, and average cost.
Read transactions (buys, sells, dividends, contributions, withdrawals, fees) with pagination, incrementally after the first full read.
Place, replace, or cancel an order. Heiwa does not do this and has no code path for it.
capabilities.permission_notes: Refused by design: the SnapTrade client issues only signed GETs against read paths, and a unit test fails if a write verb or trading path is added to it.

capabilities.description: Deposit, withdraw, or transfer money. Heiwa does not do this and has no code path for it.
capabilities.permission_notes: Refused by design; money movement stays with the user in their brokerage's own app.
